metadata.name: Todo List
metadata.description: Executes a finite caller-owned checklist sequentially with minimal orchestration. It materializes one canonical domain-neutral guide before intake, requires every substantive agent responsibility to read it, and keeps checklist, evidence, progress, revision and authority rules in one source without suppressing requested inventories, metrics or log analysis. It accepts an already supplied typed task list or gathers one bounded list, separates content ownership from dependency ordering, derives total and one-based cursor in the engine, projects exactly the current task, advances only after concise verified evidence, and asks for no approval between items. A guarded mid-run revision preserves completed positions and resumes from an explicit task number while the engine recomputes derived state. Todo List intentionally has no plan-design review, per-item retry budget, recovery protocol, aggregate result report or final semantic reviewer. Choose it when the caller already knows the checklist and needs durable cursor progress; use Quick Task when a bounded task needs planning and independent review, Robust Task for retry/recovery and critical work, or Software Development Flow for repository implementation.

nodes.directive:
Read `./moira-ws/todo-list-{{executionId}}/workflow-guide.md`, the user's complete request, and applicable primary sources. Obtain the complete authoritative ordered checklist under that guide.

Reuse a caller-supplied schema-valid task array when one is already present; otherwise plan the checklist once. If no valid dependency order exists, report the exact cycle to the author and do not submit an invalid checklist. Do not execute any task in this step.

Return `tasks` and replace `progress_checklist_outcome` with a concise bounded synopsis of the authoritative checklist. Do not predict execution or treat the synopsis as proof that work is complete.

Keep the completed positional prefix unchanged in meaning and change only unfinished work. Do not use this jump to escape a task that is merely hard, blocked, or failing.

workflow_guide.description: Canonical domain-neutral Todo List checklist, evidence, revision, record-boundary, and authority guide.
workflow_guide.default:
# Todo List guide

These rules define outcomes for a general Todo List run. A rule that does not apply to the current task is already satisfied and requires no artifact or evidence of inapplicability.

## Preserve content while ordering work

A caller-supplied schema-valid checklist keeps every item, its wording, and its scope; nothing is dropped or added. The executor may reorder unfinished items so each prerequisite exists before its consumer, must expose that reordering before work starts, and must report a real dependency cycle instead of silently choosing an invalid order. Content and order are separate responsibilities: freezing written order can execute work before its prerequisites, while rewriting content silently changes the caller's request.

A remark that governs several items remains a constraint on those items rather than becoming decorative work of its own. When no ready checklist exists, create the complete bounded checklist once without executing it. Each item carries enough goal, applicable constraint, and observable expected result to be executable on its own, but does not repeat unrelated shared doctrine; unconditional redundancy creates drifting copies and turns the checklist into the deliverable.

## Complete and evidence the real task

Perform the projected task under its actual requirements and verify the expected result before reporting success. Evidence names the concrete observation that distinguishes completion from a plausible incomplete state; a success-shaped acknowledgement without that observation can advance the cursor while the work remains undone. A blocked or incomplete task remains current and is reported truthfully rather than submitted as success.

## Keep process records useful

Checklist items contain the work, its applicable constraints, and its expected result. Evidence contains the result and distinguishing observation. Progress contains only the bounded current synopsis needed by the user. Exclude tool transcripts, copied raw output, search history, timings, hashes, decorative command/file/action inventories, activity diaries, and nonfunctional volume counts because they do not help a later reader execute, route, or judge the task.

An inventory, metric, test count, log analysis, or similar material remains valid when it is the requested domain result. Only incidental process narration about producing it is excluded; otherwise an anti-noise rule would silently narrow the caller's task.

## Revise by positional identity

Use checklist revision only when the checklist itself no longer describes the required remaining work, never to escape a task that is merely hard, blocked, or failing. Preserve completed items at their original positions and unchanged in meaning, change only the unfinished tail, and return the first position that still requires execution. Position is task identity; changing the completed prefix or restarting it loses reliable knowledge of what has already happened.

Replace checklist and progress state atomically with the new truth, retaining only a latest completed outcome that remains true. The engine derives totals, projection indices, and cursors from the checklist and resume position; parallel IDs, counts, statuses, result codes, or histories can disagree with the route and make resumption ambiguous.

## Preserve authority

The originating request is the authority ceiling. Checklist acquisition, autonomous execution, or tool availability does not authorize unrelated publication, destructive action, environment change, deployment, or version-control work. This prevents a convenient tool or a broad task description from becoming permission for a different external effect.
